topic.name: Volumes of Revolution Using the Washer Method: Rotation About Other Axes

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $x=\dfrac 6 y$ and $x=7- y$ for $y\in[1,6]$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about the line $x=-3.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.explanation:
Let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $x=\dfrac{6}{y},$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $x=7-y.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=7-y.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{1}^{6} \big[\: \left(\color{blue}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{1}^{6} \big[\: \left(\color{blue}{7-y}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-3}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{1}^{6} \left[ 10-y \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=\dfrac{6}{y}.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{1}^{6} \big[\: \left(\color{brown}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{1}^{6} \left[\: \left(\color{brown}{\dfrac{6}{y}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-3}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{1}^{6} \left[\dfrac{6}{y}+3\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{1}^{6} \left[ 10-y \right]^2 \, \textrm{d}y - \pi \int_{1}^{6} \left[ \dfrac{6}{y}+3 \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{1}^{6} \left( \left[ 10 -y \right]^2 - \left[ \dfrac{6}{y}+3 \right]^2 \right) \textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

example.title: Identifying an Integral Representing the Volume of a Solid Generated by Rotation About a Vertical Line

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $x=-\dfrac{10}{y}$ and $x= y- 7$ for $y\in[2,5]$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about the line $x=-1.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.explanation:
Let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $x=-\dfrac{10}{y},$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $x=y-7.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=y-7.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{2}^{5} \big[\: \left(\color{black}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{blue}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{2}^{5} \big[\: \left(\color{black}{-1}\right) - \left(\color{blue}{y-7}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{2}^{5} \left[ 6-y\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=-\dfrac{10}{y}.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{2}^{5} \big[\: \left(\color{black}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{brown}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{2}^{5} \left[\: \left(\color{black}{-1}\right) - \left(\color{brown}{-\dfrac{10}{y}}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{2}^{5} \left[\dfrac{10}{y}-1\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{2}^{5} \left[ 6-y \right]^2 \, \textrm{d}y - \pi \int_{2}^{5} \left[ \dfrac{10}{y}-1 \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{2}^{5} \left( \left[ 6-y \right]^2 - \left[ \dfrac{10}{y}-1 \right]^2 \right) \textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

example.title: Identifying an Integral Representing the Volume of a Solid Generated by Rotation About a Vertical Line

question.text: The region above enclosed by the curves $y=\sqrt{x}$ and $y=x^2$ for $x \in [0,1]$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $y=-1.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $y=x^2,$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $y=\sqrt{x}.$

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=\sqrt{x}.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left({\color{brown}{\textrm{upper}}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{lower}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left({\color{brown}{\sqrt{x}}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-1}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[\sqrt{x}+1\right]^2\,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=x^2.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left({\color{blue}{\textrm{upper}}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{lower}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left({\color{blue}{x^2}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-1}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[x^2+1\right]^2\,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{brown}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{blue}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[\sqrt{x}+1\right]^2 \, \textrm{d}x - \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[x^2+1\right]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_0^1 \left(\left(\sqrt{x}+1\right)^2 - \left(x^2+1\right)^2\right)\,\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_0^1 \left(2\sqrt{x}-x^4-2x^2+x\right)\,\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \pi \left.\left(\frac{4}{3}x^{3/2}-\frac{1}{5}x^5-\frac{2}{3}x^3+\frac{1}{2}x^2\right)\right|_0^1\\[5pt] & = \pi \left[\left(\frac{4}{3}(1)^{3/2}-\frac{1}{5}(1)^5-\frac{2}{3}(1)^3+\frac{1}{2}(1)^2\right)-0\right]\\[5pt] & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \frac{29\pi}{30}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Volume of a Solid Generated by Rotation About a Horizontal Line

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $x=y^2+2$ and $y=x-4$ for $y \in [-1,2]$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $x=-2.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, since we are rotating about a vertical axis, we need to solve the equation of our second curve for $x{:}$

\begin{align*} y &= x-4 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x = y+4 \end{align*}

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $x=y^2+2,$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $x=y+4.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=y+4.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \big[\: \left(\color{blue}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[\: \left(\color{blue}{y+4}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-2}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[ y+6 \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=y^2+2.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \big[\: \left(\color{brown}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[\: \left(\color{brown}{y^2+2}\right) - \left(\color{black}{{-2}}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[ y^2+4 \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of our solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_{-1}^2 \left( \left[ y+6 \right]^2 - \left[ y^2+4 \right]^2 \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_{-1}^2 \left( y^2 + 12y + 36 - (y^4 +8y^2 + 16) \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_{-1}^2 \left( 12y + 20 - y^4 - 7y^2 \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] & = \pi\left. \left( 6y^2 + 20y - \dfrac{y^5}{5} - \dfrac{7y^3}{3} \right) \right|_{-1}^2 \\[5pt] & = \pi \left[\! \left( 6\cdot2^2 + 20\cdot2 - \dfrac{2^5}{5} - \dfrac{7\cdot2^3}{3} \right) \!- \!\left( 6 - 20 + \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{7}{3} \right)\! \right] \\[5pt] & = \pi \left( \dfrac{584}{15} - \left(-\dfrac{172}{15}\right) \right) \\[5pt] & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{252\pi}{5}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Volume of a Solid Generated by Rotation About a Vertical Line

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $x=y^2-2$ and $x=y$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $x=3.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, to determine the limits of integration, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

\begin{align*} y^2-2 &= y \\[5pt] y^2-y-2 &= 0 \\[5pt] (y-2)(y+1) &= 0 \\[5pt] y &= -1,2 \end{align*}

Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=-1$ to $y=2.$

Next, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $x=y,$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $x=y^2-2.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=y^2-2.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \big[\: \left({\color{black}{\textrm{right}}}\right) - \left({\color{brown}{\textrm{left}}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[\: \left({\color{black}{3}}\right) - \left({\color{brown}{y^2-2}}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[5-y^2\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=y.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \big[\: \left({\color{black}{\textrm{right}}}\right) - \left({\color{blue}{\textrm{left}}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[\: \left({\color{black}{3}}\right) - \left({\color{blue}{y}}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[3-y\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{brown}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{blue}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left(\left[5-y^2\right]^2 - \left[3-y\right]^2\right)\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left(\left(25-10y^2+y^4\right) - \left(9-6y+y^2\right)\right)\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left(y^4-11y^2+6y+16\right)\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi\left.\left(\dfrac{y^5}{5}-\dfrac{11y^3}{3}+3y^2+16y\right)\right|_{-1}^{2} \\[5pt] &= \pi\left[\left(\dfrac{2^5}{5}-\dfrac{11(2^3)}{3}+3(2^2)+16(2)\right) - \left(-\dfrac{1}{5}+\dfrac{11}{3}+3-16\right)\right] \\[5pt] &= \pi\left[\dfrac{316}{15} - \left(-\dfrac{143}{15}\right)\right] \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{153\pi}{5}}. \end{align*}
